coverage.notes: Two weeks of a semester-long lab. Each of the first two labs has a written handout ending in a report checklist, and each has a completed report, so the report format is specified rather than guessed, but later labs (Simulink, hardware) may add requirements that are not here. The Week 3 folder holds only an empty outline and no handout. Methods cover MATLAB scripting and the closed-form second-order response; nothing on transfer-function toolbox work, Simulink, or physical-rig measurement. No syllabus was found. MATLAB conventions live in the shared MATLAB tool pack. The host cannot execute MATLAB, so results in a drafted report stay unverified until the student runs the m-file and returns its output.

course_policy.summary: No syllabus for this lab was found, so its policy on AI use is unknown. Both lab handouts separately require each student to write and run their own MATLAB files; that is an individual-work rule, not an AI policy.

pipeline_support.note: The report is a docx, which the renderer supports. Nothing executes MATLAB: the figures and every number in the report come from the student running the m-file. The rendered report can be checked for format, but its results are unverified until the student returns the printed check values and the figure, and a deliverable must not be called ready before then.

sections.rule: Section headings follow the current handout's checklist. Lab 1 asks for three: Objectives, Results & Analysis, Conclusion. Lab 2 asks for four, adding Procedure between Objectives and Results & Analysis. Results & Analysis is subdivided per experiment.
sections.note: Do not merge the two lists. A lab whose handout is silent defaults to the most recent handout's list; tell the student that is an assumption.

objectives.rule: One paragraph of complete sentences in the student's own words. No numbering, no bullets, not copied from the handout. The conclusion answers these objectives.

procedure.rule: When required (Lab 2 onward), a picture of the system studied and the equation that characterizes it, plus a short description of what the m-file does, pointing to the code appendix.

results_and_analysis.rule: One subsection per experiment. Refer to results by figure and table number to support each claim. The analysis explains the physics behind the plots, not only what they show.
results_and_analysis.basis: Lab 2 guidelines content checklist; both submitted reports.

question_answers.rule: Where a handout poses numbered questions inside an experiment, restate each question and answer it directly under that experiment's subsection.
question_answers.basis: Lab 1 handout (Experiments 1 and 7); the Week 1 submitted report.

methods.title: Second-order transient response across damping regimes
methods.when: A lab asks how the damping ratio shapes the free or step response of a mass-spring-damper or any second-order system.
steps: Write the governing ODE from a force balance and name the parameters: M, b, k.
Express the response through the natural frequency and damping ratio, both defined from M, b, k.
Pick one value in each regime the handout lists: undamped, underdamped, critically damped (just below 1 when the closed form divides by sqrt(1 - zeta^2)), overdamped.
Compute all cases in one m-file (see the shared MATLAB pack, closed-form-parameter-sweep).
Tie each regime to its poles, the roots of s^2 + 2 zeta wn s + wn^2: the real part sets decay, the imaginary part sets oscillation.
Check a number with a closed form against the plot, such as the ratio of successive extrema in the underdamped case.
Explain why the overdamped response is slower than the critically damped one rather than treating it as an error.
pitfalls: The complex branch of acos past zeta = 1, which can flip the sign of the overdamped curve.
Describing the plots without the physics: the checklist asks how M, b, k and zeta produce the behavior.
Envelope overlays drawn in a line style another curve already uses, which collide in grayscale.
methods.basis: Lab 2 guidelines (experiments and content checklist); the Week 2 submitted report and m-file; the Week 2 output-check notes.

methods.title: Supporting mathematics
methods.when: Lab 1's math review, and any later lab that needs it.
steps: Partial fractions: factor the denominator, then solve for residues; check by recombining.
Quadratic roots by formula, written as -a +/- b j for complex pairs.
Block reduction to one polynomial numerator over one polynomial denominator: the transfer-function form.
Complex numbers as vectors for sums and differences, and in polar form (magnitude and angle).
Convergence: a decaying exponential reaches steady state; a growing one does not.
pitfalls: Leaving a simplified transfer function with a fraction inside the numerator or denominator.
methods.basis: Lab 1 handout (Experiment 8); the Week 1 submitted report.

assignment_families.title: Weekly MATLAB lab report
stages: read the assigned textbook sections and handout
write and run the m-file in lab, individually
write the report in Word from the saved files
upload the report and the m-files before the next lab
deliverables: Word report with the sections the handout's checklist names
the m-file(s), uploaded separately and also included in the report
what_good_looks_like: Objectives as one rephrased paragraph, not a copied list.
A procedure that shows the system diagram and its governing equation, and points to the code appendix.
Every figure produced by the script unedited, readable in grayscale, captioned below and referred to by number.
Analysis that explains the behavior through the physics and the math, referring to figures and tables for support.
A conclusion that answers each objective.
The code, header filled in, in the report and uploaded.
assignment_families.basis: Lab 1 handout and Lab 2 guidelines report checklists; the Week 1 and Week 2 submitted reports.
